plans.architecture: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN (Manager/vManage, OMP, TLOC, app-aware routing, SIG/SASE, centralized+localized policy, ZTP, controller redundancy, Multi-Region Fabric, MPLS-to-SD-WAN coexistence)
plans.headline: The entire SD-WAN overlay is collection-blind: COLLECT_PARSE_V3_23_0.py emits zero `show sdwan ...` commands, so parse/analyze/detect have nothing to read — fabric health (control connections, OMP, BFD, app-route, trackers) is structurally unobservable and the 14 SD-WAN doctrine entries stay WHY-only with no HOW. First build the collector+parsers (P1) or every downstream detector starves.

build_plan.item: Add the Catalyst SD-WAN show-command set to the live/offline collection command lists so every downstream layer has evidence to read. Add: show sdwan control connections, control connection-history, control local-properties, control valid-vsmarts/valid-teps, control summary, bfd sessions, bfd summary, bfd history, bfd tloc-summary-list, omp peers, omp summary, omp routes, omp tlocs, omp services, system status, policy from-vsmart, policy access-list-counters, app-route stats, app-route sla-class, tunnel statistics, ipsec inbound/outbound-connections, endpoint-tracker, secure-internet-gateway tunnels, certificate {serial-numbers/validity/root-ca-cert}, reboot history, version. Gate them to detected SD-WAN platforms (IOS-XE-SDWAN edge + Manager/Controller/Validator) so non-SD-WAN fleets skip them. Accept BOTH new doc names and legacy CLI tokens (vsmart/vbond) per the post-2024 rename.
build_plan.canonical_check: All control/data/overlay/policy/security axes; evidence-honesty: state lives only on Manager/controllers/live edges, so collect it or mark axes not-observed

build_plan.item: parse_sdwan_control_connections / parse_sdwan_control_history / parse_sdwan_local_properties — parse PEER TYPE (vsmart/vbond/vmanage), peer system-ip/site-id, STATE (up/down), and from connection-history the LOCAL ERROR / REMOTE ERROR columns (NOERR vs CRTVERFL/CTORGNMMIS/BIDNTVRFD/DCONFAIL/DHSTMO); from local-properties pull organization-name, certificate-status, root-ca-chain-status, system-ip/site-id/domain-id, NAT type, and expected-vsmarts. Follow the existing `parse_<thing>(output: str) -> Dict/List[Dict]` shape in parse.py.
build_plan.canonical_check: Control-plane redundancy (controllers per edge vs expected) + control connection DOWN/flapping diagnosable cause (cert/org-name/board-id/DTLS/clock)

build_plan.item: parse_sdwan_bfd_sessions / parse_sdwan_bfd_summary — per-session SRC/DST TLOC, COLOR, STATE (up/down/NA), transitions count, encap; and sessions-up vs total from summary. Reconcile DST color-pairs to TLOC inventory so a missing BFD on an advertised color is detectable.
build_plan.canonical_check: BFD sessions DOWN/NA or excessive transitions = data-plane blackhole/flapping tunnel even when control is up (UDP 12346/port-hop blocked, NAT, MTU/IPsec)

build_plan.item: parse_sdwan_omp_peers / parse_sdwan_omp_summary / parse_sdwan_omp_routes_tlocs — OMP peer STATE + R(received)/I(installed)/S(sent) counters per vSmart; from summary admin/oper-state, vsmart-peers, graceful-restart status+timer, send-path-limit, ecmp-limit; from routes/tlocs the equal-cost path count per prefix and TLOC presence.
build_plan.canonical_check: OMP peering incomplete / route propagation broken (received=0 while sent>0); GR disabled; send-path-limit/ecmp-limit capped at default 4 vs available paths

build_plan.item: parse_sdwan_tloc_summary — per-TLOC system-ip + color + encapsulation(ipsec/gre), preference/weight, and per-site color count + edge count (from tloc-summary-list / local-properties), so single-transport / single-homed sites are computable. Capture PMTU and active/standby per color.
build_plan.canonical_check: Single-homed sites / single transport (one edge or one TLOC color) — the dominant brownfield fragility class for dual-transport SD-WAN

build_plan.item: parse_sdwan_app_route_stats / parse_sdwan_sla_class / parse_sdwan_from_vsmart — per app-route Index: mean-loss/mean-latency/mean-jitter by local-color/remote-color; SLA-class thresholds (loss/latency/jitter); and from policy from-vsmart the presence of control-policy / app-route-policy / TLOC-lists / vpn-membership / advertised service-routes.
build_plan.canonical_check: AAR not enforcing SLA (tunnels exceed SLA class, no backup meeting SLA, poll default 10m vs enhanced 10s) + centralized/control policy missing/asymmetric/service-chain next-hop absent

build_plan.item: parse_sdwan_sig_tunnels / parse_sdwan_endpoint_tracker — SIG auto-tunnel list (provider, HA active/backup pair, tunnel state) joined to endpoint-tracker status (up/down) + RTT vs SLA + presence; flag SIG tunnels with NO tracker and no DIA fallback.
build_plan.canonical_check: SIG/SASE egress fragile: SIG tunnel without tracker / without HA pair / no DIA fallback blackholes all internet-bound traffic (SIG has no implicit tracker)

build_plan.item: parse_sdwan_certificate / parse_sdwan_system_status — cert validity window + serial allow-list + root-CA presence; per-component NOS train (Manager/Controller/Validator/edge) and chassis/serial. Feeds ZTP-readiness and version-vs-advisory and compatibility-matrix (control-components must be >= edge).
build_plan.canonical_check: ZTP/PKI bootstrap readiness (cert validity, serial/chassis allow-list, root-CA chain) + software not current vs advisories / edge newer than its controllers

build_plan.item: compute_sdwan_fabric_health — analysis axis that folds the parsed control/OMP/BFD/TLOC state into a per-fabric signal block: controllers-per-edge vs expected, BFD up/total, OMP peer up + received/installed, per-site TLOC color & edge counts, GR/ecmp settings, control-connection error taxonomy. Emits the `sig[...]` keys the detectors consume (mirrors how _d_vpc_health reads sig['vpc_*']). Must mark each sub-axis 'not observed' when the underlying show output is absent — never infer fabric health from edge running-config alone.
build_plan.canonical_check: Aggregates control-redundancy / OMP / BFD / single-homed / GR / ECMP checks into detector-ready signals; bare-config false-health guard

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_control_redundancy — detector (engine_actionable) firing when distinct Controllers(vsmart) or Validators(vbond) == 1, a Manager cluster is an even/non-quorum node count, controllers share one transport/site, OR an edge has fewer control connections than expected-vsmarts (max-control-connections capping redundancy). Returns _decision with priority High, citing show-sdwan-control-connections fields + valid-vsmarts.
build_plan.canonical_check: Control-plane underbuilt/non-redundant controllers (single Controller/Validator, even Manager quorum, co-located) + edge connected to only one Controller

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_bfd_health — detector (engine_actionable) firing on any BFD session down/NA on an advertised color-pair or high-transition flapping; reports blackholed/unstable transports per site with src/dst TLOC+color, distinguishing 'control up but data-plane down'. Priority High.
build_plan.canonical_check: BFD sessions DOWN/NA or excessive transitions = data-plane blackhole / flapping tunnel

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_omp_health — detector (engine_actionable) firing on OMP peer not up, routes received=0/installed=0 while sent>0, GR disabled, or send-path-limit/ecmp-limit left at default 4 while more equal-cost TLOC paths exist. Priority High (peering/propagation) / Med (path-limit, GR). Cites omp peers R/I/S + omp summary.
build_plan.canonical_check: OMP peering incomplete/route propagation broken + ECMP/path-redundancy capped + graceful-restart disabled/misaligned

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_control_diag — detector (engine_actionable) translating connection-history LOCAL/REMOTE ERROR codes + local-properties into named root causes (CRTVERFL=cert/root-CA, CTORGNMMIS=org-name mismatch, BIDNTVRFD=board-id, serial-not-in-allowlist, DCONFAIL/DHSTMO=DTLS, clock skew) for any down/flapping control connection. Priority High.
build_plan.canonical_check: Control connection DOWN/flapping with a diagnosable cause (the classic 'edge won't join fabric' root causes)

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_single_homed — detector (engine_actionable) firing on any site with one WAN Edge or one TLOC color (e.g. MPLS-only, no biz-internet). Priority High. Cites per-site TLOC color/edge counts from tloc-summary + local-properties.
build_plan.canonical_check: Single-homed sites / single transport — no transport diversity / no edge HA

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_aar_sla — detector firing when app-route stats persistently breach the SLA class with no backup path meeting SLA, AAR policy absent in from-vsmart, or poll-interval at legacy 10m where 10s enhanced AAR is warranted. Priority Med.
build_plan.canonical_check: App-Aware Routing not enforcing SLA / persistent SLA breach with no compliant backup

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_sig_resilience — detector firing on a SIG/SASE tunnel without an endpoint/tracker, without an HA active/backup pair, or with no DIA fallback-to-routing. Priority High. Cites sig tunnels + endpoint-tracker presence/state.
build_plan.canonical_check: SIG/SASE internet egress fragile (no tracker / no HA pair / no DIA fallback blackholes internet traffic)

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_software_currency — detector firing when a component's NOS train is behind a recommended train / open-advisory, OR an edge is newer than its controllers (compatibility-matrix violation: control-components must be >= edge). Surface 'advisory surface OPEN' wording, never 'release vulnerable'; reuse the existing software_risk/eoldb posture vocabulary. Priority High.
build_plan.canonical_check: Software not current vs advisories / mixed-incompatible Manager-Controller-Validator-edge versions (edge newer than controllers)

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_ztp_pki — detector firing on cert validity nearing/after expiry, root-CA chain missing, org-name mismatch, or serial/chassis not in the authorized allow-list (ZTP/Validator mutual-trust readiness). Priority Med. Cites show sdwan certificate + local-properties.
build_plan.canonical_check: Zero-touch provisioning / PKI bootstrap readiness (vBond mutual-trust, cert validity, serial allow-list)

build_plan.item: _d_sdwan_mgmt_isolation + _d_sdwan_crypto_aaa — hardening detectors: (a) VPN0 transport not behind a perimeter / VPN512 mgmt not strictly OOB / mgmt ports (22/443/830) internet-exposed; (b) weak DH groups 1/2/5 (removed 17.11.1a+), SSH SHA-1/weak ciphers, SNMPv1/v2, self-signed Manager web cert, FIPS off on 20.15.1+ defaults, local-only AAA / over-broad netadmin / no syslog. Reuse existing _d_harden/_d_mgmt scaffolding. Priority High (isolation) / Med (crypto/AAA).
build_plan.canonical_check: Management/transport isolation broken + weak crypto/cipher posture + AAA/RBAC/audit gaps

build_plan.item: SD-WAN fixtures + honesty/golden tests — captured `show sdwan ...` sample outputs (control connections incl. error codes, bfd sessions up+down, omp peers with R/I/S, tloc summary single-homed case, app-route SLA breach, sig tunnel w/o tracker, cert) as parser fixtures; plus a tests/test_sdwan_*.py locking (1) each parser's shape, (2) each detector fires on the bad fixture and stays silent on a clean one, (3) the not-observed invariant: when no `show sdwan` output is present every SD-WAN axis is 'not observed', NOT 'healthy' (bare-config false-health guard), and (4) all SD-WAN doctrine stays engine_actionable=False while the new detectors are engine_actionable=True.
build_plan.canonical_check: Evidence-honesty / not-observed-never-healthy across all checks; proposer != verifier

build_plan.item: Design/CRD/MOP/HLD SD-WAN sections fed by the new detectors — extend the design_blueprint -> design.docx Target-State Design Recommendations to emit SD-WAN decision rows (today zero), add CRD requirement rows (introduce-controller-redundancy / enforce-dual-transport / remediate-BFD / SIG-tracker / version-uplift) in the BCP-14 traceability matrix, and an MOP/runbook cutover-coexistence section (MPLS-to-SD-WAN hybrid: VRF/site-id conflict scan, BGP/OSPF-into-OMP redistribution, phased per-region wave blast-radius). Keep the 14 reference doctrine entries as WHY; these add the HOW. Do NOT duplicate the doctrine text.
build_plan.file_target: cisco_toolkit/design.py + crd.py + mop.py + runbook.py (new SD-WAN sections gated on SD-WAN evidence present)
build_plan.canonical_check: Centralized policy / migration coexistence / control redundancy surfaced as recommended ACTIONS (HOW), reconciled single-source from the detectors

build_plan.item: compute_sdwan_migration_coexistence — analysis axis for MPLS-to-SD-WAN hybrid interworking: detect VRF name/ID conflicts between legacy and overlay, BGP/OSPF redistribution-into-OMP points, and build per-region phased-wave move-groups with blast-radius (which sites lose policy/reachability if a wave's controller/edge is touched). Feeds the MOP coexistence section above and the explorer blast-radius. Lower priority — needs both legacy and overlay state collected.
build_plan.canonical_check: Migration coexistence validation (hybrid overlay interworking, VRF conflicts, redistribution-into-OMP, phased wave cutover blast-radius)

plans.architecture: SP / MPLS core (L3VPN RFC 4364 + L2VPN/EVPN over SR-MPLS or LDP/RSVP-TE, SR + TI-LFA RFC 9855, inter-AS A/B/C/AB, MVPN Rosen/NG-MVPN, with SRv6 uSID as the emerging variant). Predominantly IOS-XR PE/P with IOS/IOS-XE edge; two strictly-layered planes (IGP+label transport vs MP-BGP service).
plans.headline: The engine collects and parses ZERO MPLS/SR/VPN state (no LFIB, no LDP/RSVP-TE, no VPNv4/v6, no EVPN, no SRGB/TI-LFA, no MVPN) — every SP-core health check is unimplementable until a collection+parser+build layer feeds new snapshot fields; the 28 sp-* KB principles are all engine_actionable:false because no data gates them.

build_plan.item: Add the SP/MPLS transport collection block to BOTH the NX-OS and IOS/XR command lists: show mpls forwarding-table / show mpls forwarding (XR), show mpls ldp neighbor detail, show mpls ldp discovery, show mpls ldp igp sync, show mpls interfaces, show mpls label table detail (XR). Gate by platform (XR vs IOS verb) and keep fail-soft so a non-MPLS box returns empty. This is the prerequisite that unblocks every P1 detector below.
build_plan.file_target: COLLECT_PARSE_V3_23_0.py (command lists ~L476-528 NX-OS, ~L532-583 IOS; add to a new SP block + register in cmd_to_file)
build_plan.canonical_check: show mpls forwarding LFIB is the core forwarding source of truth; show mpls ldp neighbor/igp sync underpins the LDP-session-down and LDP-IGP-sync checks

build_plan.item: parse_mpls_forwarding_table(output) -> [{prefix, local_label, out_label(Pop/Unlabelled/Aggregate/<n>), out_iface, next_hop}] handling BOTH 'show mpls forwarding-table' (IOS) and 'show mpls forwarding' (XR) column layouts. The single most load-bearing parser: the LFIB is what every transport-continuity and label-stack check reads.
build_plan.canonical_check: BGP-free core / transport-label continuity — a VPN next-hop /32 must resolve to a labeled end-to-end path; detect Unlabelled/Pop-too-early in the LFIB

build_plan.item: parse_mpls_ldp_neighbors(output) -> [{peer_id, state(Oper/up/down), discovery_sources, targeted, holdtime, session_protection(bool)}] from 'show mpls ldp neighbor detail'; plus parse_mpls_ldp_igp_sync(output) -> [{iface, sync_achieved(bool)}] from 'show mpls ldp igp sync'.
build_plan.canonical_check: LDP session down/flapping; LDP-IGP synchronization missing (Sync not achieved while link in IGP forwarding -> transient black-hole on link-up); LDP session protection absent on redundant core

build_plan.item: build_mpls_transport(cmd_to_file) -> {lfib:[...], ldp_neighbors:[...], ldp_igp_sync:[...], mpls_interfaces:[...]} mirroring build_routing_neighbors: parse-from-already-collected, _safe_parse fail-soft, empty dict when no MPLS. Then key it into the snapshot dict (COLLECT_PARSE ~L2018/2071 alongside routing_neighbors) as snap['mpls_transport'].
build_plan.file_target: cisco_toolkit/build.py (append after build_routing_neighbors L136) + COLLECT_PARSE_V3_23_0.py:2071 snapshot assembly
build_plan.canonical_check: Establishes the canonical mpls_transport snapshot field the whole detector layer reads (one-source-of-truth join), matching the existing routing_neighbors pattern

build_plan.item: _d_mpls_lsp_health(snap, sig): coverage-honest detector firing only when snap['mpls_transport'] is non-empty. Flags (a) LDP neighbors not Oper/up, (b) LFIB prefixes with Unlabelled/no out-label for known PE loopbacks, (c) LDP sessions without session-protection on a node with parallel core paths. 'Not observed' never becomes 'healthy' (guard like _d_false_health).
build_plan.canonical_check: LDP session down + transport-label continuity broken + LDP session protection absent

build_plan.item: Add the MP-BGP service-plane collection: show bgp vpnv4 unicast summary, show bgp vpnv6 unicast summary, show bgp l2vpn evpn summary, show bgp vpnv4 unicast vrf all labels, show vrf detail (XR: show vrf all detail). Platform-gated, fail-soft.
build_plan.canonical_check: MP-BGP VPNv4/VPNv6/EVPN session down or RR SPOF; RT/RD design fault; provides the per-VRF + RD/RT evidence for the L3VPN integrity detector

build_plan.item: parse_bgp_vpnv4_summary(output) (and reuse for vpnv6/evpn AFI by passing the AFI label) -> [{neighbor, as, state(Established/...), pfx_rcd(int), tbl_ver, is_rr_client}]. parse_vrf_detail(output) -> {vrf: {rd, import_rt:[...], export_rt:[...], interfaces:[...]}} — the SSOT for RD/RT reconciliation.
build_plan.canonical_check: VPNv4/v6/EVPN session state != Established or PfxRcd stuck/0; single-RR SPOF; RD/RT import-export reconciliation across the two PEs of a VPN

build_plan.item: build_vpn_service(cmd_to_file) -> {vpnv4:[...], vpnv6:[...], evpn:[...], vrfs:{...}} fail-soft, keyed into snapshot as snap['vpn_service']; extend build_routing_neighbors / parse_*_neighbors to capture a per-VRF context tag so customer OSPF/EIGRP at a PE-CE edge is not misattributed as internal core IGP.
build_plan.file_target: cisco_toolkit/build.py (build_vpn_service + VRF tag in build_routing_neighbors L125) + COLLECT_PARSE snapshot assembly
build_plan.canonical_check: VRF/PE-CE routing-table segmentation context (med gap) — distinguish PE/CE from campus core; feeds the RD/RT and inter-AS detectors

build_plan.item: _d_vpn_rd_rt_integrity(snap, sig): fires only when snap['vpn_service'].vrfs present. Detects (a) VPNv4/v6/EVPN sessions not Established or PfxRcd=0, (b) single RR neighbor (no redundancy), (c) asymmetric/mistyped import vs export RT across PEs of the same VPN, (d) duplicate RD where unique-RD-per-VRF-per-PE is needed for BGP best-path/PIC. Cite the field/line per finding.
build_plan.canonical_check: MP-BGP session down / RR SPOF + Route-Target/RD design fault (asymmetric RT = route leak or missing routes; same RD reused)

build_plan.item: Add Segment-Routing + TI-LFA collection: show segment-routing mpls (XR) / show isis segment-routing, show isis segment-routing label table / show ospf segment-routing, show route <PE-loopback> + show cef <PE-loopback> detail (repair/backup presence), show isis fast-reroute summary. Platform-gated, fail-soft.
build_plan.canonical_check: Non-homogeneous SRGB / prefix-SID conflict; TI-LFA/FRR leaving prefixes unprotected (no Backup TI-LFA repair next-hop)

build_plan.item: parse_segment_routing_sids(output) -> {srgb_base, srgb_range, prefix_sids:[{prefix, sid_index, label}], adj_sids:[...]} and parse_ti_lfa_coverage(output) -> [{prefix, protected(bool), repair_type(TI-LFA/none), backup_next_hop}] from show route/show isis fast-reroute. Capture per-node SRGB so homogeneity can be diffed fleet-wide.
build_plan.canonical_check: Homogeneous SRGB across the domain (heterogeneous = design smell, resize needs reload, SRGB_ALLOC_FAIL); TI-LFA per-prefix repair present

build_plan.item: _d_sr_srgb_homogeneity(snap, sig): diff parsed SRGB base/range across all SR-capable nodes; flag any node whose SRGB differs from the fleet mode, plus duplicate/overlapping prefix-SID indices. Coverage-honest: only fires when >=1 node reports an SRGB.
build_plan.canonical_check: Non-homogeneous SRGB or prefix-SID conflict breaks label-stack consistency / can fail SR programming

build_plan.item: _d_fhrp_election(snap, sig): fires when a peer-joined group has (a) equal priorities across peers (default 100/100 — non-deterministic election), or (b) HSRP/GLBP preempt OFF so the primary never reclaims after recovery, or (c) priority gap smaller than the largest track decrement (a tracked-object failure cannot flip the election). Reads snap['fhrp_config']; add no_fhrp_election count to _signals().
build_plan.canonical_check: Priority mis-set / no differentiation + preempt missing: intended primary must have highest priority AND (priority_primary - sum_decrements) < priority_secondary, with preempt explicit on HSRP/GLBP.

build_plan.item: _d_fhrp_tracking(snap, sig): fires when an Active/Master group at an L2/L3 boundary has NO track object wired (untracked active gateway black-holes on uplink loss), OR a track object exists but no group subscribes (dead config), OR a subscribed tracked object is DOWN while the group is still Active. Joins snap['fhrp_config'].tracks with parsed 'show track' state (already collected, COLLECT_PARSE:573).
build_plan.canonical_check: No interface/object tracking on the active gateway = classic silent outage; tracked object must be actually referenced by the group (show track subscriber list non-empty).

build_plan.item: parse_show_track(output) -> {obj_id: {type(ip-sla|interface|route|list), state(Up|Down), delay, subscribers:[group...]}}: structured parser for 'show track'/'show track brief'. build_plan.canonical_check: show track proves tracking is actually WIRED to the group (subscriber list) and the object is Up/Down — an Up object nothing tracks is dead config.

build_plan.item: _d_fhrp_peer_consistency(snap, sig): fires on any peer mismatch within a joined group — HSRP v1-vs-v2 (vMAC-prefix/version differs → both go active), virtual-IP mismatch (DIFFVIP class), timer asymmetry (hello/hold differ → inconsistent failover), or authentication type/key mismatch (BADAUTH → groups separate). Reads snap['fhrp_config']; this is the structured-detail superset of today's brief-only mixed-proto/different-VIP checks in compute_fhrp_consistency.
build_plan.canonical_check: Peer consistency: version, group#, VIP, vMAC, timers and auth must be identical on every peer — any mismatch = two-active / no-redundancy / silent split-brain.

build_plan.item: _d_fhrp_authentication(snap, sig): fires when a gateway group has (a) no authentication at all on customer/edge segments, (b) cleartext text-auth (sent unencrypted, trailing-space-fragile), or (c) auth type/string mismatch across peers. Severity Medium (security/availability). Reads snap['fhrp_config'].auth_type/auth_key_present.
build_plan.canonical_check: Authentication missing/mismatched/cleartext: best practice MD5 key-string/key-chain consistently on all peers; flag none, text, or per-peer mismatch (%HSRP-4-BADAUTH).

build_plan.item: _d_fhrp_vpc_alignment(snap, sig): correlates snap['fhrp_config'] with the EXISTING snap['vpc'] (parse_vpc, parse.py:515; _d_vpc_health, design_advisor.py:992) — fires when in a vPC fabric the FHRP-active peer is NOT the primary vPC peer, OR 'peer-gateway' is absent (no active/active data plane for the VIP), OR 'use-bia'/manual vMAC is present (breaks vPC load-balancing), OR aggressive (non-default) FHRP timers are tuned on vPC peers. No FHRP↔vPC join exists today.
build_plan.canonical_check: vPC-specific: primary vPC peer = FHRP-active highest-priority, peer-gateway enabled, never use-bia/manual vMAC, default timers mandated (BFD-for-FHRP unsupported under vPC).

build_plan.canonical_check: Single/non-redundant RP; RPF failure; >2 Anycast RPs without MSDP mesh-group; SSM/IGMPv3; rogue-RP hardening (all best_practice_checks depend on these inputs existing)

Parse 'show ip rpf <ip>' (RPF interface / RPF neighbor / 'failed') and extend mroute parsing to flag (*,G)/(S,G) entries whose 'Incoming interface: Null' or RPF nbr 0.0.0.0. build_plan.file_target: cisco_toolkit/parse.py (new fn; extend parse_multicast_info IIF capture at :1536-1542)
build_plan.canonical_check: RPF failure — mroute incoming-interface Null or 'show ip rpf' returns no/incorrect interface (the single most common multicast data-plane outage)

build_plan.item: parse_msdp_state(peer_out, sa_cache_out) -> {peers:[{peer_ip, state, sa_rcv, sa_sent, resets}], n_sa_cache, originator_id, mesh_group_present}. Parse 'show ip msdp peer' (State Up/Down, SA counts) + 'show ip msdp sa-cache' count + running 'ip msdp mesh-group'/'ip msdp originator-id'. Required to validate Anycast-RP redundancy liveness — currently no MSDP visibility at all.
build_plan.canonical_check: >2 Anycast RPs without MSDP mesh-group / Anycast pair with MSDP down so (S,G) state is not shared; MSDP SA plane unhardened (sa-filter/sa-limit/originator-id)

build_plan.item: parse_pim_neighbor(neigh_out) + parse_igmp_interface(igmp_if_out): per-interface PIM neighbor list (neighbor IP, DR-priority, holdtime) and IGMP version (v2/v3) + on-segment querier. Feeds DR-election, neighbor-gap, and the SSM-without-IGMPv3 check. Today the engine knows PIM mode per interface but not neighbor adjacency or IGMP version.
build_plan.canonical_check: SSM group-range without IGMPv3 (receivers IGMPv2); PIM neighbor adjacency gaps / DR election

build_plan.item: parse_igmp_snooping_mrouter(out) -> [{vlan, mrouter_ports:[...], learn_mode}]. Parse 'show ip igmp snooping mrouter'. This is the missing half of the querier-gap logic: a VLAN with ZERO mrouter ports AND no querier is the true L2-island outage; with an mrouter port present the SVI/PIM router is reachable so it is NOT a gap.
build_plan.canonical_check: L2 VLAN with snooping enabled but NO querier AND NO mrouter port — membership ages out and multicast stops/floods

build_plan.item: Assemble the new parsed records into service_map.multicast: extend the collection loop and compute_service_map to thread pim_rp_state, rpf, msdp, pim_neighbors, igmp_interface (version), and snooping_mrouter per device — mirroring how igmp_queriers/classified_groups are already gathered (COLLECT_PARSE :1577-1595 builds the per-device dicts; compute_service_map :1637-1648 packs the 'multicast' dict). New keys: multicast.rp, multicast.rpf, multicast.msdp, multicast.mrouter, multicast.igmp_versions.
build_plan.canonical_check: Coverage-honesty: assemble evidence before deriving findings; one source of truth for RP/MSDP/RPF state

build_plan.item: Extend compute_multicast_intelligence with an RP-redundancy analyzer: classify RP architecture (single static RP=SPOF / Anycast with N RPs / Phantom-RP Bidir / BSR), and emit risks: single-static-RP (High, total outage on RP loss), Anycast loopback not /32 (High, host-route ambiguity — cross-check rp_ip against SVI/loopback mask in interface data), >2 Anycast RPs without MSDP mesh-group (High), MSDP peer Down with empty sa-cache (High), overlapping/inconsistent C-RP group ranges (High). Today compute_multicast_intelligence (:1712) handles only MAC-alias/querier/PTP.
build_plan.file_target: cisco_toolkit/analyze.py (compute_multicast_intelligence :1712-1808, new risk block + summary keys)
build_plan.canonical_check: Single/non-redundant RP; Anycast loopback not /32; >2 Anycast RPs without MSDP mesh-group; inconsistent/overlapping C-RP ranges

build_plan.item: Add an RPF-integrity detector to compute_multicast_intelligence: emit 'rpf-failure' risk (High) for any (*,G)/(S,G) with Null incoming-interface or failed 'show ip rpf', citing the group and target; and an 'rp-unreachable' risk when an RP address has no matching route/RPF. This is the highest-value new detection (the #1 multicast outage) and is wholly absent.
build_plan.canonical_check: RPF failure (Null IIF / rpf failed / missing route to source/RP) — single most common multicast outage

build_plan.item: Add a PIM-mode-vs-group-range detector: cross-reference per-interface PIM mode (already parsed) and parsed SSM/RP ranges against observed group addresses. Emit risks: dense-mode/sparse-dense-mode left enabled (Medium, flooding/fallback — flag 'Dense'/'Sparse-Dense' from multicast_info), SSM range (232/8 or configured) overlapping an RP/SM group-range (High), and an SM group with no RP serving its range (Medium). Uses data the engine already has plus the new RP ranges.
build_plan.canonical_check: Dense-mode/sparse-dense left enabled or no RP for an SM group; SSM range overlapping an RP/SM range

build_plan.item: Upgrade the querier-gap detector to be coverage-honest and mrouter-aware. Currently gap_vlans is derived ONLY from collected SVIs carrying multicast_info (:1756-1765), so an L2 island whose SVI sits on an UNCOLLECTED L3 core can never be flagged — and 'no querier observed' silently reads as fine. Reconcile each endpoint-bearing VLAN: querier present -> OK; querier absent + mrouter port present -> covered by router; querier absent + no mrouter + SVI uncollected -> emit UNKNOWN (uncollected-upstream), never 'healthy'; querier absent + no mrouter + multicast-active -> High gap. Encode the canonical caveat #4.
build_plan.canonical_check: L2 VLAN snooping-on, no querier, no mrouter = stops/floods; coverage-honesty — 'no querier observed' must be UNKNOWN when L3 core uncollected, never healthy

build_plan.item: Add a colliding/mis-anchored querier detector: flag (a) two queriers seen in one VLAN, (b) a configured snooping-querier IP equal to the VLAN SVI/HSRP VIP (cross-check igmp_queriers[].querier against SVI/HSRP addresses) — querier election is lowest-IP and self-disables on a lower query, so collisions cause membership flap. Extends the existing querier model (which only records presence).
build_plan.canonical_check: Multiple/colliding IGMP-snooping queriers or querier IP colliding with SVI/VIP — membership flap / intermittent loss

build_plan.item: Add a multicast control-plane hardening detector reading the new running-config section: flag absence of 'ip pim accept-rp', 'ip pim accept-register', 'ip pim rp-announce-filter' (Auto-RP), 'ip pim bsr-border' at edges, 'ip pim neighbor-filter', 'ip multicast boundary [filter-autorp]' (admin-scoped 239/8), and 'ip pim register-rate-limit'. Per the Cisco Multicast Security Toolkit. No multicast security posture is assessed today.
build_plan.file_target: cisco_toolkit/analyze.py (compute_multicast_intelligence, or fold into config-security-auditor surface)
build_plan.canonical_check: No rogue-RP/RP-spoof protection; no admin multicast scoping at boundaries; RP register-bomb / no register-rate-limit

build_plan.item: Add an HSRP-aware-PIM detector: where HSRP/VRRP is configured on an SVI that also runs PIM, flag missing 'ip pim redundancy ... dr-priority' / PIM DR not aligned to the HSRP-active gateway (cross-reference existing FHRP/HSRP model against PIM DR-priority from parse_pim_neighbor). The engine already tracks FHRP; this joins it to the multicast DR.
build_plan.file_target: cisco_toolkit/analyze.py (compute_multicast_intelligence; reuse FHRP data already in the model)
build_plan.canonical_check: First-hop/last-hop gateway redundancy not multicast-aware (HSRP failover but PIM DR stays put → duplicate/dropped streams)

build_plan.item: Add a Bidir Phantom-RP correctness detector: when Bidir RP ranges are present (parse 'ip pim rp-address ... bidir' / 'ip pim bidir-enable'), verify the phantom address is UNASSIGNED and the two DF-candidate loopbacks differ in prefix length (/30 vs /31) so the active root is deterministic. Niche but a documented fatal Bidir smell.
build_plan.canonical_check: Bidir-PIM Phantom-RP misconfigured (phantom assigned, or equal-length loopbacks → non-deterministic root)

build_plan.item: Add a VXLAN-EVPN/TRM underlay-multicast detector (NX-OS): when VXLAN/NVE evidence is present, verify underlay RP is PIM-SM with spine Anycast-RP and that L2VNI/L3VNI-to-multicast-group mapping is consistent across leafs; flag MSDP-down on border-leaf and missing/inconsistent VNI->mcast-group config. Requires 'show fabric multicast'/'show nve peers' added to NX-OS collection. The canonical model explicitly scopes TRM as the current DC default.
build_plan.canonical_check: VXLAN-EVPN/TRM underlay RP or group mapping broken (underlay not PIM-SM, spine Anycast-RP/MSDP down, VNI mcast-group inconsistency)

build_plan.item: IPv6 multicast / MLD twin: add a separate FF00::/8 regex and parse_mld_groups() + parse_mld_snooping_querier(), thread into service_map.multicast as v6 counterparts, and extend the querier-gap + SSM(FF3x::/32 + MLDv2) checks for IPv6. All current parsing is scoped to IPv4 class-D only.
build_plan.file_target: cisco_toolkit/parse.py (new _MCAST6_RE + parsers near :1554) + analyze.py service_map assembly
build_plan.canonical_check: IPv6 multicast (FF3x::/32 SSM with MLDv2) parity — SSM without MLDv2 is a hard misconfig

build_plan.item: Extend design_advisor signature + the _d_mcast detector. In design_advisor.py extract the new multicast_intelligence summary fields (rp_architecture, n_rp_redundancy_risks, n_rpf_failures, n_msdp_down) into sig (alongside querier_gaps/mcast_risks at :218-220), and split _d_mcast (:769) into distinct High-priority design decisions: 'multicast-rp-redundancy' (introduce Anycast-RP + MSDP / dual-RP when single static RP) and 'multicast-rpf-integrity' separate from the existing L2-edge/querier decision, each citing the new evidence paths.
build_plan.canonical_check: Single/non-redundant RP → design must introduce Anycast-RP+MSDP; RPF integrity surfaced as a design action

build_plan.item: Expand CRD requirements (currently only REQ-T-MC-001 'preserve multicast delivery', crd.py:291-296). Add: REQ-T-MC-002 RP redundancy — provide >=2 RPs via Anycast-RP+MSDP (or Phantom-RP for Bidir), no single static RP, Anycast loopback /32 (adaptive: introduce-when-absent, mirroring how the FHRP REQ was made adaptive); REQ-T-MC-003 RPF/unicast-symmetry — every (S,G) has a valid incoming interface; REQ-T-MC-004 SSM ranges require IGMPv3/MLDv2; REQ-T-MC-005 multicast security baseline (accept-rp/accept-register/boundary). Each evidence-gated and coverage-honest (UNKNOWN when RP/MSDP uncollected).
build_plan.canonical_check: Single/non-redundant RP; RPF failure; SSM/IGMPv3; rogue-RP hardening — all surfaced as customer requirements

build_plan.item: Extend the Excel write_multicast_intelligence_sheet (excel.py:1094) and runbook §6.6 (runbook.py:450-510) with RP/MSDP/RPF sections: an 'RP architecture & redundancy' block (method, RP list, redundancy verdict, MSDP peer states), an 'RPF integrity' block (Null-IIF groups, failed RPF checks), and an 'L2 snooping reconciliation' table (per-VLAN querier vs mrouter vs UNKNOWN-uncollected). These render the new analysis into the workbook + DOCX deliverables.
build_plan.canonical_check: Coverage-honest reporting of RP redundancy / RPF / per-VLAN querier-vs-mrouter (UNKNOWN never silently healthy)

build_plan.item: Add parse-level fixtures + tests for the new parsers: sample 'show ip pim rp mapping' (Auto-RP, BSR, static, Anycast /32, Bidir), 'show ip rpf' (success + 'failed'), mroute with Null IIF, 'show ip msdp peer' (Up + Down), 'show ip msdp sa-cache' (populated + empty), 'show ip igmp snooping mrouter' (with/without ports), 'show ip igmp interface' (v2 vs v3). Lock parser output shapes in a new test module mirroring tests/test_multicast_intel.py.
build_plan.canonical_check: RP discovery/redundancy; RPF; MSDP liveness; mrouter reconciliation; SSM/IGMPv3 — parser-locked

build_plan.item: Add detector-level + coverage-honesty tests: assert single-static-RP -> SPOF risk; Anycast non-/32 -> risk; MSDP-down+empty-cache -> risk; Null-IIF -> rpf-failure risk; SSM-without-IGMPv3 -> risk; and a mutation/refutation test that a VLAN with no querier AND an UNCOLLECTED SVI yields UNKNOWN (not 'healthy') — guarding the false-health regression class the canonical caveat #4 calls out. Include an emit-invariant test that all new risks carry severity + standard citation.
build_plan.canonical_check: Coverage-honesty — 'no querier/RP observed' is UNKNOWN when upstream uncollected, never healthy; every consequential output evidence-grounded

plans.architecture: QoS & media transport (trust boundaries, classification/marking, queuing/scheduling, voice/video edge, PTP boundary-clock)
plans.headline: The engine audits QoS/PTP INTENT (running-config) only and never reconciles it against RUN-STATE — none of the decisive operational commands (show policy-map interface, show queuing interface, show ptp brief/port/corrections, interface drop counters) are even collected, so the 'configured-but-ASIC-rejected / unbounded-LLQ / trust-on-wrong-port / PTP-up-but-not-locked' false-health classes are structurally invisible.

build_plan.item: Add run-state QoS + PTP commands to BOTH collection lists (COMMANDS_NXOS ~L505-530, COMMANDS_IOS ~L532-584): 'show policy-map interface', 'show policy-map interface brief', 'show queuing interface' (NX-OS) / 'show platform hardware ... qos' guarded, 'show ptp brief', 'show ptp port interface', 'show ptp corrections', 'show interfaces counters errors'. This is the gating prerequisite — every run-state parser/detector below is inert until these land. Mark SLOW where needed; per-interface variants iterate the interface list like existing per-if collection.
build_plan.canonical_check: Reconcile INTENT (running-config) against RUN-STATE (show policy-map interface / show queuing interface / show ptp clock|corrections) — never infer health from config alone

build_plan.item: parse_policy_map_content(text): extend the running-config QoS parse to capture, per policy-map, each class's match criteria (match dscp/cos/qos-group/access-group), marking actions (set ip dscp / set dscp / set cos / set qos-group), policer (police rate / conform / exceed), and priority/bandwidth/bandwidth-remaining/shape/random-detect. Today parse_qos_config (parse.py:2214-2279) records only policy-map NAMES and child refs — there is no substrate for marking or LLQ validation. Return the per-class structure keyed by policy-map; tolerant, never raises.
build_plan.canonical_check: Voice priority queue has NO policer (unbounded LLQ) — a strict-priority class with no police can starve all other classes under congestion

build_plan.item: parse_policy_map_interface(output): NEW run-state parser for 'show policy-map interface <if>' — per-(interface,direction,class) offered rate, drop counters, priority/police conform/exceed/drop, and whether the policy is actually attached. Feeds the configured-vs-active reconciliation (the marquee false-health class). {} on absent output.
build_plan.canonical_check: Service-policy configured but NOT applied / silently rejected by ASIC-TCAM — policy in running-config but show policy-map interface shows it not attached or zeroed (configured ≠ active)

build_plan.item: _d_qos_marking / extend compute_qos_audit (analyze.py:4264-4390) to validate marking values against the RFC 4594-as-adapted-by-Cisco medianet table: EF=46 voice, CS3=24 call-signaling (NOT CS5 — encode Cisco's deliberate deviation), AF41=34 multimedia/interactive-video, CS5=40 broadcast-video, CS6=48 network-control, CS1=8 scavenger. Read the new per-class structure; flag mismatched set-dscp values. Add a doctrine kind to _QOS_DOCTRINE (analyze.py:4234).
build_plan.canonical_check: DSCP marking values violate the RFC 4594 / medianet model (voice not EF46, signaling not CS3, video not AF41, broadcast not CS5, scavenger not CS1)

build_plan.item: _d_unbounded_llq detector (analyze.py, new _QOS_DOCTRINE kind): firing when a parsed policy-map has a 'priority' class with no 'police' (IOS LLQ) / a NX-OS priority qos-group with no conforming type-qos policer. Pure on parse_policy_map_content output; cite the policy-map + class.
build_plan.canonical_check: Voice priority queue has NO policer (unbounded LLQ) — Cisco mandates the priority queue be policed at a configured rate

build_plan.item: Platform-dialect branching in parse_qos_config / compute_qos_audit: branch QoS interpretation by NOS family so a Catalyst-9000 fleet is not false-negatived. Legacy IOS/Cat-OS = 'mls qos' + srr-queue/wrr-queue/priority-queue out; IOS-XE Cat9000 = MQC-only (no global 'mls qos' enable — QoS is on-attach) + 'trust device' + AutoQos-4.0-* macros; NX-OS = three-tier type qos / type network-qos / type queuing with ≤4 qos-groups. Gate the existing 'no-trust-boundary' (mls-qos-based) finding to legacy IOS only. Needs platform identity already in the model (parse_show_version).
build_plan.canonical_check: QoS not enabled / default-pass on legacy IOS (global mls qos OFF by default makes all trust/queue config inert) — platform-scoped to legacy IOS only; Cat9000 IOS-XE is MQC-on-attach

build_plan.item: _d_conditional_trust detector: flag voice-VLAN access ports lacking conditional trust ('trust device cisco-phone' IOS-XE / 'mls qos trust device cisco-phone' IOS) AND lacking an ingress marking policy — phone EF markings reset to DF on ingress. Today compute_qos_audit emits the broader 'voice-without-qos' but does not distinguish the conditional-trust idiom specifically; refine the existing finding's detail to name the missing conditional-trust statement.
build_plan.canonical_check: Conditional trust missing at the phone edge — voice ports with no 'trust device cisco-phone' so phone markings are reset to DF and voice loses EF end-to-end

build_plan.item: parse_ptp_brief(output) + parse_ptp_port(output): NEW run-state parsers extracting per-port PTP role (MASTER/SLAVE/PASSIVE/DISABLED/FAULTY), peer, announce/sync/delay-req intervals, and delay mechanism (E2E vs P2P). Today parse_ptp_clock (parse.py:1597-1648) gives device-type/offset/GM only — no port role. {} on absent output.
build_plan.canonical_check: PTP port stuck in PASSIVE/FAULTY or unexpected MASTER — a port that should be SLAVE-to-GM is PASSIVE/FAULTY, or a leaf is erroneously MASTER (lost upstream)

build_plan.item: _d_ptp_role / extend compute_ptp_readiness (analyze.py:1651-1688) with run-state port-role findings: PASSIVE/FAULTY ports on a media path, a leaf gone MASTER, and on NX-OS a non-boundary device-type (transparent-clock is unsupported on Nexus 9000 — boundary-clock only). compute_ptp_readiness today reports only operational-vs-dormant counts; add role-aware findings from the new parsers. Do NOT rebuild the existing dormant/operational logic.
build_plan.canonical_check: PTP running in a non-boundary mode on Nexus, or PTP port stuck PASSIVE/FAULTY/unexpected-MASTER (Nexus 9000 = boundary-clock only; transparent unsupported)

build_plan.item: parse_ptp_corrections(output): NEW parser for 'show ptp corrections' — the last-N correction-sample histogram per slave port (max/mean magnitude). Feeds an SLA-band check: nominal = tens of ns; alarm approaching ~10000 ns. Today only a binary |offset|<1us 'locked' flag exists (parse.py:1639) — no jitter/trend/band. {} on absent output.
build_plan.canonical_check: PTP offset-from-master / corrections out of spec (drift) — corrections show microseconds instead of tens of ns; must be <~10000 ns / within the 2000-sample window

build_plan.item: _d_ptp_drift detector (analyze.py, in compute_ptp_readiness or compute_multicast_intelligence ptp_tree): flag offset-from-master / corrections magnitude exceeding the tens-of-ns nominal band (warn) and approaching 10000 ns (high). Reads parse_ptp_corrections + offset_ns.
build_plan.canonical_check: PTP offset-from-master / corrections out of spec — persistent large corrections = clock-role instability or transport asymmetry

build_plan.item: _d_ptp_gm_consistency detector: extend compute_multicast_intelligence ptp_tree (analyze.py:1769-1774 already collects grandmasters[]) to flag mixed PTP domain numbers across the fabric, multiple competing GMs without redundancy/priority discipline, and low GM clock-class/accuracy (holdover/free-run). The data (domain, grandmaster, clock-identity) is parsed but no cross-device consistency/redundancy audit exists.
build_plan.canonical_check: PTP grandmaster / domain inconsistency — mixed domain numbers, multiple competing GMs, mismatched priority1/2 causing BMCA flaps, or low GM clock-class

build_plan.item: _d_trust_path_consistency detector: cross-interface audit that distribution/core/uplink ports TRUST the DSCP the access layer marked (Cisco model = mark at access, trust through dist/core, reclassify only at WAN edge). Flag uplink/core ports that are untrusted or remark. Also flag inconsistent trust within a voice-VLAN/broadcast group (one port trusts DSCP, another untrusted). compute_qos_audit is per-device only (analyze.py:4264-4390) — no cross-interface/cross-path consistency pass exists.
build_plan.canonical_check: Trust/marking inconsistent across the path (DSCP not preserved hop-to-hop) — core/uplink ports re-mark or fail to trust DSCP the access layer set

build_plan.item: Video/multimedia edge classification in compute_qos_audit: classify edges beyond voice — IP-camera/surveillance/interactive-video ports (heuristic: AF41/CS5 marking on the port, video-capable endpoint via CDP/LLDP, or a video VLAN) and map them to their own RFC 4594 queuing requirement (interactive video bandwidth/delay/jitter distinct from voice). Today only n_voice_if is counted (analyze.py:4298) — video edges are invisible. Add n_video_if and a doctrine finding for video edges with no video queue.
build_plan.canonical_check: AutoQoS 'voip cisco-phone' applied to a VIDEO endpoint collapses AF41 video into the voice profile; interactive video needs its own RFC 4594 class, not the voice profile

build_plan.item: _d_egress_drops detector: correlate parsed interface output-drop / total-output-drops / queue-drops (from 'show interface'/'show interfaces counters errors', already collected) with the ABSENCE of an egress service-policy (IOS-XE) / type-queuing policy (NX-OS) — rising drops + no egress policy = default tail-drop, real-time media is collateral. Requires the per-interface drop counters to be surfaced into the model.
build_plan.canonical_check: No egress queuing policy / default tail-drop on congested links — interface with output drops and no service-policy output → all classes tail-drop equally

build_plan.item: NX-OS system-QoS structural checks in compute_qos_audit: parse 'system qos' / 'show policy-map system' to verify ≤4 user system-classes (qos-groups) and SPQ placement on the HIGHEST qos-group (single SPQ = qos-group 3). Flag >4 classes or priority on a low qos-group (silently fails to prioritize). Needs parse_policy_map_content to also handle type-queuing/system-qos and the global_attach already captured (parse.py:2208-2262).
build_plan.canonical_check: NX-OS 4-class / SPQ-placement errors — >4 qos-groups or strict-priority on the wrong (non-highest) qos-group

build_plan.item: PTP profile + IPFM target-architecture validation: validate the parsed PTP profile (parse_ptp_clock already extracts profile, parse.py:1617) is the media/broadcast profile (SMPTE ST 2059-2) not the enterprise profile on media-path boundary clocks; and detect NDFC IPFM / non-blocking-media (PIM + flow provisioning) as the modern DC-media target vs classic per-hop DSCP. Add as findings + a design-doctrine note.
build_plan.canonical_check: PTP profile validation (enterprise vs broadcast ST 2059-2) on media-path clocks; for DC media fabrics detect IPFM/non-blocking-media vs classic DSCP

build_plan.item: _d_copp detector: parse/detect Control Plane Policing — NX-OS 'service-policy type control-plane' / copp-system-* on 'control-plane', and IOS CoPP — to flag a media fabric with no control-plane protection (DoS exposure). parse_qos_config already sees directionless global_attach (parse.py:2259-2262) but does not classify control-plane policy specifically; the existing dangling-ref logic deliberately ignores copp-system- names (analyze.py:4356-4358), so CoPP presence/absence is currently unjudged.
build_plan.canonical_check: No control-plane QoS (CoPP) — missing protection against control-plane DoS on the media fabric

build_plan.item: _d_cac detector + design note: at a bandwidth-limited WAN voice edge, flag a priority/police voice policy with NO Call Admission Control on the call-control side (CUCM Locations / RSVP / call-manager-fallback / gateway dial-peer CAC) — over-subscription degrades ALL active calls, not just call N+1. Detection is heuristic (priority voice + WAN edge + no CAC keywords); render primarily as a design-doctrine requirement.
build_plan.canonical_check: No Call Admission Control at the voice gateway/CUCM over a bandwidth-limited WAN — LLQ caps the queue but without CAC an over-subscribed call count degrades all calls

build_plan.item: _d_scavenger_wan detector: at the SP/PE handoff flag (a) scavenger CS1 not policed down and (b) WAN-edge egress not remarking to the SP-agreed DSCP/EXP subset (SP bleaches/honors only a CoS/EXP subset, so enterprise markings are lost). Reads parse_policy_map_content on the WAN-edge egress policy.
build_plan.canonical_check: Scavenger/bulk not de-prioritized & no DSCP-trust on the WAN handoff to SP — no CS1 policer; PE-facing egress not remarking to SP-honored values

build_plan.item: SD-WAN QoS-model detection: when the WAN edge is Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN (formerly Viptela), detect that the QoS model is per-VPN app-aware-SLA forwarding-classes (OMP/policy) rather than classic LLQ, and suppress/relabel classic-LLQ findings on those interfaces so the assessment does not mis-flag a correctly-built SD-WAN edge. Reference-only doctrine plus a guard in the LLQ/marking detectors.
build_plan.canonical_check: If the WAN edge is Catalyst SD-WAN, QoS = per-VPN app-aware-SLA forwarding-classes, not classic LLQ — that distinction must be detected (currency: Viptela→Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN)

build_plan.item: _d_st2022_7 dual-path detector: verify ST 2110 essence flows (Broadcast-AV groups) are dual-homed on independent paths for ST 2022-7 seamless protection — flag on-air multicast groups whose receiver/source ports have no redundant independent path. Reuse the existing link/SPOF model (analyze.py _physical_uplink_index) keyed to on_air groups from compute_multicast_intelligence (already flags on_air, analyze.py:1739).
build_plan.canonical_check: No dual-path / redundant-link validation for ST 2022-7 media (seamless protection) — ST 2110 essence flows must be dual-homed on independent synchronized paths

build_plan.item: PTP-vs-multicast co-location audit: combine compute_ptp_readiness and compute_multicast_intelligence (currently separate, analyze.py:1651-1688 and 1712-1808) to verify media domains (ST 2110 + Dante groups) are BOTH on boundary-clock switches — timing and reachability co-location. Add to compute_multicast_intelligence risks.

plans.architecture: Classic Cisco WAN overlays — DMVPN (mGRE/NHRP/IPsec), GETVPN (GDOI + COOP key servers), FlexVPN (IKEv2), IWAN/PfRv3 app-aware path selection, and the eBGP/IGP edge they ride on (IOS/IOS-XE autonomous, non-SD-WAN). Brownfield assessment of this stack is normally a MIGRATION-READINESS exercise toward Catalyst SD-WAN.
plans.headline: Zero overlay-control evidence is collected — no show dmvpn/ip nhrp/crypto session/crypto gdoi/domain master output exists, so every DMVPN/GETVPN/FlexVPN/PfRv3 health verdict is structurally UNKNOWN; the P1 fix is adding the collection set, without which no parser or detector below can run honestly.

build_plan.item: Add the WAN-overlay collection set to BOTH command lists (COMMANDS_IOS, and COMMANDS_NXOS where a verb exists): show dmvpn detail, show ip nhrp detail, show ip nhrp nhs detail, show crypto session detail, show crypto ipsec sa, show crypto isakmp sa, show crypto ikev2 sa detailed, show crypto gdoi, show crypto gdoi ks coop, show crypto gdoi ks members, show crypto gdoi gm replay, show domain <name> master status, show domain <name> border channels, show crypto ipsec transform-set, show crypto ikev2 proposal, show interfaces tunnel, show bfd neighbors. These are show-STATE not in a default show-run grab — without them every signal below is UNKNOWN, never healthy.
build_plan.canonical_check: COVERAGE-HONESTY: NHRP/GDOI/PfR/crypto are not in show run+show version; uncollected => redundancy/anti-replay/path-control UNKNOWN, never healthy.

build_plan.item: parse_crypto_session(): 'show crypto session [detail]' -> per-peer [{peer, ivrf, fvrf, status, uptime, ike_sa, ipsec_flows}]. Status UP-ACTIVE = up; anything else (DOWN/NEGOTIATING) = not up. The fastest 'is the tunnel actually up' triage. Do NOT duplicate parse_bgp_summary/parse_bgp_table — those already exist.
build_plan.canonical_check: show crypto session status UP-ACTIVE evidences a live tunnel; absence/other state = tunnel not up.

build_plan.item: parse_crypto_ipsec_sa(): 'show crypto ipsec sa' -> per peer/interface [{peer, local, remote, pkts_encaps, pkts_decaps, send_errors, recv_errors, pfs_group, path_mtu, in_spi, out_spi, transform}]. Carries the encaps/decaps counters and path_mtu needed for the one-way black-hole and MTU detectors.
build_plan.canonical_check: IPsec one-way/black-hole: #pkts encaps rising while #pkts decaps=0 (or mirror) + non-zero send/recv errors.

build_plan.item: parse_dmvpn(): 'show dmvpn detail' + 'show ip nhrp nhs detail' -> per-tunnel [{tunnel, peers:[{nbma, tunnel_addr, attr_flags(D/S/I), state(UP/DOWN/NHRP)}], nhs_state(RE/E/DOWN), peer_count, nhrp_group}]. The primary DMVPN health structure; NHS state and incomplete(I) entries drive the registration-failure detector.
build_plan.canonical_check: DMVPN NHRP registration failure / NHS down: NHS not RE; hub cache has no/incomplete(I) spoke entries.

build_plan.item: parse_crypto_algorithms(): scan 'show crypto ipsec transform-set' + 'show crypto ikev2 proposal' + 'show crypto isakmp policy' (and run-config crypto) -> {host: [{context, encryption, integrity, dh_group}]} normalizing weak tokens (esp-des/esp-3des/esp-null, md5/sha1, dh 1|2|5). Feeds the weak-crypto + FN72510 upgrade-blocker detector. Reuse, do NOT replace, the existing analyze.py IKEv1 regex (crypto isakmp policy) which is security-surface only.
build_plan.canonical_check: Weak/deprecated crypto: DES/3DES/esp-null, MD5/SHA1, DH 1/2/5 — negotiates today but FN72510 breaks it on IOS-XE 17.11.1+ upgrade.

build_plan.item: parse_gdoi(): 'show crypto gdoi' + 'show crypto gdoi ks coop' + 'show crypto gdoi ks members' + 'show crypto gdoi gm replay' -> {host:{role(KS/GM), group, registered(bool), coop:[{priority, role(Primary/Secondary), peer_reachable}], member_count, tbar_errors, pseudotime}}. The structure behind every GETVPN detector (COOP split-brain, GM-never-registered/fail-open, TBAR skew).
build_plan.canonical_check: GETVPN COOP split-brain (two Primary / unreachable peer KS) and GM fail-open (registration failed -> cleartext on a should-be-encrypted WAN).

build_plan.item: parse_pfrv3(): 'show domain <name> master status' + 'show domain <name> border channels' + 'show domain <name> master traffic-classes summary' -> {domain, master_status, borders:[{up, wan_path, channels:[{reachable, oop, loss, delay, jitter}]}], traffic_classes:[{controlled(bool), exit}]}. Evidences whether PfRv3 is actually steering traffic or has silently fallen back to routing.
build_plan.canonical_check: PfRv3 not controlling traffic: MC-BR down / site-prefix unlearned / all channels OOP -> silently reverts to underlying routing path.

build_plan.item: parse_bgp_neighbor_policy(): 'show ip bgp neighbors <x>' -> per-neighbor {inbound_route_map, outbound_route_map, inbound_prefix_list, outbound_prefix_list, max_prefix, ttl_security/min_ttl(GTSM), bfd_enabled}. Extends existing parse_bgp_summary (state/PfxRcd only) to the EDGE-POLICY surface — filtering, max-prefix, GTSM, BFD — none of which is parsed today.
build_plan.canonical_check: BGP edge missing in/out prefix-filtering, maximum-prefix, and ttl-security (GTSM) -> hijack/transit-leak + RIB-exhaustion + spoofed-179 DoS exposure.

Parse BOTH dialects: IOS-XE `show policy-map interface control-plane` (per-class conform/exceed/violate bytes+drops) and NX-OS `show policy-map type control-plane` (copp-system-class-* ConformedBytes/ViolatedBytes/Dropped). Empty output => {} so absence is distinguishable from zero-drops. Tolerant; never raises; no counters fabricated.
build_plan.canonical_check: CoPP present but actively starving the control plane — sustained violate/exceed drops on legitimate classes (BGP/OSPF/EIGRP/HSRP/SSH/SNMP/ARP/ICMP).

build_plan.item:
parse_copp_status(output) -> {profile: strict|moderate|lenient|dense|none, applied:bool, diff_lines:[...]}. NX-OS `show copp status` (which default profile is applied / 'No CoPP policy') + `show copp diff profile

applied` (non-empty drift from default). Distinguishes 'profile=none at setup' (open supervisor) from a healthy applied profile.

plans.architecture: Management & Assurance plane — model-driven management (NETCONF/RESTCONF/gNMI), Model-Driven Telemetry (dial-out + dial-in), and the classic syslog/NTP/AAA-for-mgmt/logging/SNMP baseline, across IOS-XE / NX-OS / IOS-XR with an assurance consumer (Catalyst Center or TIG/gNMIc).
plans.headline: Model-Driven Telemetry + programmatic management (NETCONF/RESTCONF/gNMI/MDT) is completely unobserved — no collection, no parser, no detector — so the engine cannot grade whether assurance is actually streaming, nor catch the config-present/pubd-dead false-health trap.

build_plan.canonical_check: Enablement & process health + dial-out SSOT integrity require the telemetry/netconf/gnmi/http and ntp-status/snmp-user output to even exist; nothing downstream is parseable until these are in the command lists.

build_plan.canonical_check: Enablement & process health (netconf-yang/pubd, gnmi secure vs insecure) + security of the mgmt surface (RESTCONF on HTTPS not plain http server; gNMI secure-server+trustpoint).

All-{} = not collected (coverage-honest, never 'healthy').
build_plan.canonical_check: Coverage & redundancy signals: a device with no telemetry evidence is 'not observed', never silently 'streaming fine'.

build_plan.item: compute_streaming_telemetry_readiness(telemetry_state): per-device + fleet roll-up detecting (a) configured-but-process-dead / receiver never Connected (false-health, HIGH); (b) receiver/transport NOT Connected — Connecting/Resolving/NA/Disconnected/Idle/Transmit-Error with rising tx-errors (HIGH); (c) single collector / no secondary destination (MED); (d) plaintext or no-AAA programmatic transport — RESTCONF on plain http server, gNMI insecure-server, no trustpoint (HIGH); (e) sample-interval mis-tuned / 0-where-periodic (LOW); (f) wrong VRF or encoding/protocol mismatch (MED). Coverage-honest 'not collected' band when no telemetry evidence. Mirror compute_platform_health band/structure; register a _run_phase in COLLECT_PARSE and add to the snapshot.

build_plan.canonical_check: Telemetry process-dead false-health + dial-out receiver-not-connected + single-collector + plaintext/unauthenticated transport + cadence/encoding/VRF mismatch — the five core MDT best-practice checks.

build_plan.item: parse_ntp_status(text) + build_ntp_status(cmd_to_file) + compute_ntp_health(): parse 'show ntp status' (sync state / stratum / offset) and 'show ntp associations [detail]' (the '*' sys.peer master, reach, per-peer stratum, configured-server count) and the 'ntp authenticate/authentication-key/trusted-key/server …key/access-group/source' config slice. Detect: UNSYNCHRONIZED / stratum-16 / no '*' master (HIGH — corrupts every telemetry+syslog timestamp); single configured server (MED); no authentication / no access-group (MED). This is depth ABOVE the existing binary 'no-ntp' presence flag in parse_security — do not re-detect mere presence.

Detect: <2 'logging host' or zero remote collector (MED — no off-box audit trail); missing 'logging source-interface' (MED); 'logging trap' too restrictive so real events drop (MED); missing 'service timestamps log datetime msec localtime show-timezone' (MED — events uncorrelatable); console/monitor logging left on (LOW — CPU spike risk). Depth ABOVE the existing buffer-content parse_syslog_events and the binary 'no-logging' flag — the engine reads what logs SAY but never whether they REACH a collector.
